props.gloss_en: Choni: Master of the world, Your children have turned to me, for I am like a member of Your household; I swear by Your great name that I will not move from here until You have mercy on Your children
rain began to trickle
his students: we have seen you and will not die [?]; it seems to us the rain falls only to release your oath
Choni: not thus did I ask, but for rain [to fill] cisterns, ditches and caves
they fell furiously, until every drop was as large as the mouth of a barrel
and the Sages estimated that no drop was less than a log
his students: it seems to us the rain falls only to destroy the world
Choni: not thus did I ask, but for rain of favour, blessing and generosity
they fell properly, until all the people went up to the Temple Mount because of the rain
they said: just as you prayed that they fall, so pray that they go away
Choni: thus have I received, that one does not pray over an excess of good
nevertheless, bring me a bull of thanksgiving; they brought it, and he laid both hands on it

Choni's prayer: Your people Israel whom You took out of Egypt can bear neither excess of good nor excess of punishment; You were angry -- they cannot stand; You showered good -- they cannot stand; may it be Your will that the rains stop and there be relief in the world
at once the wind blew, the clouds scattered, the sun shone, and the people went out to the field and brought back truffles and mushrooms

Shimon ben Shatach: were you not Choni, I would decree a ban on you; for were these years like Elijah's, when the keys of rain were in his hand, would not the name of Heaven be desecrated through you?

but what can I do to you, for you importune the Omnipresent and He does your will, as a son importunes his father and he does his will (wash me in hot water, rinse me in cold, give me nuts, almonds, peaches and pomegranates -- and he gives)
and of you the verse says: 'your father and your mother will rejoice, and she who bore you will be glad' (Prov 23:25)
what the Chamber of Hewn Stone sent Choni: 'you shall decree a thing and it shall be established for you, and light shall shine on your ways' (Job 22:28)
'you shall decree a thing' -- you decreed below, and the Holy One fulfils your word above
'and light shall shine on your ways' -- a generation that was dark you lit with your prayer
'when they are cast down, you shall say: lift up' (Job 22:29) -- a generation that was low you raised with your prayer
'and the humble person he will save' -- a generation bowed in its sin you saved with your prayer

'he will deliver the one who is not innocent' (Job 22:30) -- a generation that was not clean you delivered with your prayer; 'he will be delivered through the cleanness of your hands' -- you delivered it through your pure deeds
all his life that righteous man was troubled by 'when the Lord returned the captivity of Zion we were like dreamers' (Ps 126:1); he said: is there anyone who sleeps seventy years in a dream?
the man planting a carob, which bears fruit after seventy years: I found the world with carobs; as my fathers planted for me, I too plant for my children
a rock-formation enclosed him, he was hidden from sight and slept seventy years; when he rose he saw a man gathering from [the carobs] -- the planter's grandson
Choni: learn from this that I have slept seventy years
the Sages in the study hall: our teachings are as clear as in the years of Choni HaMe'aggel, for when he entered the study hall he would resolve every difficulty the Sages had
he said: I am he; they did not believe him, and did not give him the honour due to him
he was distressed, prayed for mercy, and died
Rava: this is what people say: either companionship or death
Abba Chilkiya was Choni's grandson; when the world needed rain the Sages would send to him, he would pray, and rain came
once they sent a pair of Sages; they found him hoeing in the field; they greeted him and he did not acknowledge them

on the way: wood and hoe on one shoulder, cloak on the other; barefoot all the way, shoes on at the water; garments lifted through thorns; his wife came out to meet him adorned; she entered first, then he, then the Sages; he ate without inviting them; he gave the elder child one loaf and the younger two
Abba Chilkiya to his wife: I know the Sages came about rain; let us go up to the roof and pray -- perhaps the Holy One will be appeased and rain will come, and we will not take credit for ourselves
he stood in one corner and she in another; the clouds rose first from his wife's corner
Abba Chilkiya: blessed is the Omnipresent, who did not make you need Abba Chilkiya
the Sages: we know the rain came because of the master; but let the master tell us these things that puzzle us
why did he not acknowledge their greeting? I was a day-labourer, and said: I must not be idle
why the wood on one shoulder and the cloak on the other? it was a borrowed cloak -- I borrowed it for this, not for that
why barefoot on the road and shod in the water? on the road I can see, in the water I cannot
why did he lift his garments through the thorns? this [the skin] heals and that [the garment] does not
why did his wife come out adorned? so that I not set my eyes on another woman
why did she enter first, then he, then they? because you are not known [tested] to me
why did he not invite them to eat? because there was not much bread, and I said: I will not make the Sages credit me for nothing
why one loaf to the elder child and two to the younger? this one stays at home, and that one sits in the synagogue
why did the clouds rise first from his wife's corner? because a woman is at home and gives bread to the poor, and her benefit is immediate; I give a coin, and its benefit is not immediate
alternatively: those hooligans in our neighbourhood -- I prayed that they die, and she prayed that they repent [and they repented]
Chanan HaNechba was Choni's daughter's son; when the world needed rain the Sages sent schoolchildren to him, who grabbed the hem of his cloak and said: Abba, Abba, give us rain
Chanan: Master of the world, act for the sake of these, who cannot tell the Abba who gives rain from the Abba who does not
why is he called Chanan HaNechba? because he would hide himself in the privy
R' Zerika to Rav Safra: come and see the difference between the mighty of the Land of Israel and the pious of Babylonia
the pious of Babylonia, Rav Huna and Rav Chisda: when the world needed rain they said: let us gather together and pray, perhaps the Holy One will be appeased and bring rain

the mighty of the Land, like R' Yona father of R' Mani: when rain was needed he told his household he was going to buy grain with a zuz; outside he stood in a deep and hidden place, covered in sackcloth, prayed, and rain came; asked at home whether he brought grain, he said: since rain came, the world is now relieved
he stood in a deep place, as it is written: 'out of the depths I have called You, O Lord' (Ps 130:1)
R' Mani his son was harassed by the house of the Nasi; he prostrated himself on his father's grave; when they passed there, their horses' legs stuck until they undertook not to harass him
R' Mani to R' Yitzchak ben Elyashiv: the rich men of my father-in-law's house harass me -- let them become poor, and they did; they press me [for support] -- let them become rich, and they did
my wife is not acceptable to me -- what is her name? Chana. Let Chana become beautiful, and she did; she is haughty toward me -- let Chana return to her blackness, and she did
to two students who asked him to pray that they become very wise: it was with me, and I sent it away
R' Yosei bar Avin used to attend R' Yosei of Yokrat; he left him and came to Rav Ashi
Shmuel (as Rav Ashi recited): one who takes a fish out of the sea on Shabbat is liable once [an area] the size of a sela on it has dried
R' Yosei bar Avin: let the master say: and [the dried area is] between its fins
Rav Ashi: does the master not hold that R' Yosei b. R' Avin said that? -- I am he
why did you leave him? a man who did not spare his son and his daughter -- how would he spare me?
his son, when the hired workers were hungry and no bread came: fig tree, fig tree, bring forth your fruit and let my father's workers eat; it did and they ate
R' Yosei of Yokrat to the workers: do not hold it against me; I was late because I was busy with a mitzva, and I walked until now
my son, you troubled your Creator to make the fig tree bring forth its fruit before its time -- may you be gathered before your time

of his beautiful daughter, at whom a man peered through a fence (if I did not merit to marry her, shall I not merit to see her?): my daughter, you are distressing people; return to your dust, and let people not stumble through you

he had a donkey hired out by day and sent home with its fee on its back; if they added or withheld, it would not come; once a pair of sandals was left on it, and it would not go until they were removed
when the charity collectors saw Elazar Ish Birta they hid from him, for he would give them all he had
Elazar Ish Birta, on his way to buy his daughter's dowry, told the collectors were for an orphan boy and girl: by the Temple service, they take precedence over my daughter
one zuz was left; he bought wheat and threw it into the granary; his wife found the granary full of wheat, pouring out through the door-socket

to his daughter (come and see what your Friend did for you): by the Temple service, they are consecrated property as far as you are concerned, and you have no more in them than one of the poor of Israel
R' Yehuda Nesia, whose fast brought no rain: how great is the distance from Samuel of Ramah to Yehuda ben Gamliel! woe to the generation so afflicted, woe to him in whose days this happened
R' Yehuda Nesia decreed a fast, prayed, and no rain came; [after his words] he was distressed, and rain came
the house of the Nasi decreed a fast and did not inform R' Yochanan and Resh Lakish; in the morning they informed them
Resh Lakish to R' Yochanan: but we did not accept it upon ourselves from the evening!
R' Yochanan: we are drawn after them
when the Nasi's fast brought no rain, Oshaya Ze'ira of the colleagues recited to them: 'and it shall be, if it was done in error by the eyes of the congregation' (Num 15:24)
a parable: a bride in her father's house -- as long as her eyes are beautiful her whole body needs no examination; if her eyes are bleary, her whole body needs examination
his [the Nasi's] servants came, put a scarf on his neck, and harassed him
the townspeople: leave him, for he distresses us too; since we see that all his deeds are for the sake of Heaven we say nothing to him and leave him be -- you too, leave him
Rebbi decreed a fast and no rain came; Ilfa (some say R' Ilfi) went down before the ark, said 'who causes the wind to blow' and a wind blew, 'who causes the rain to fall' and rain came
asked by Rebbi what his deeds were: I live in a poor village with no wine for kiddush and havdala; I take the trouble to bring wine for kiddush and havdala and discharge their obligation
Rav came to a place, decreed a fast and no rain came; the prayer leader went down, said 'who causes the wind to blow' and a wind blew, 'who causes the rain to fall' and rain came

asked by Rav what his deeds were: I teach children, I teach the children of the poor as the children of the rich, and from whoever cannot pay I take nothing; I have a fish pond, and whoever is negligent I bribe with fish and coax him until he comes and reads
Rav Nachman decreed a fast, prayed, and no rain came; he said: take Nachman and throw him from the wall to the ground; he was distressed, and rain came
Rabbah decreed a fast and no rain came; they said to him: but when Rav Yehuda decreed a fast, rain came!

Rabbah: if it is because of learning, we surpass them: in Rav Yehuda's years all the learning was in Nezikin, and we learn all six orders; when Rav Yehuda reached Uktzin (the woman who pickles vegetables in a pot / olives pickled with their leaves) he said: I see here the disputes of Rav and Shmuel; and we learn Uktzin in thirteen yeshivot
yet Rav Yehuda, when he removed one shoe, rain came; and we cry out all day and no one pays attention to us
if it is because of deeds -- if anyone has seen anything [wrong in me], let him say; but what can the great of the generation do when their generation is not worthy?
Rav Yehuda saw two men throwing bread at each other; he said: learn from this that there is plenty in the world; he cast his eye -- and there was famine

led out by Rav Kahana his attendant past the market, he saw a crowd at a basket of dates on sale and said: learn from this there is famine in the world; he told his attendant: remove my shoes; he removed one shoe and rain came
Elijah came and said: the Holy One said: if you remove the other, I will destroy the world
Rav Mari son of Shmuel's daughter: I was standing on the bank of the Pappa river, and saw angels in the guise of sailors bringing sand and filling ships with it, and it became fine flour
I told them: do not buy from this, for it is the work of miracles; tomorrow ships of wheat will come from Parzina
Rava came to Hagronia, decreed a fast and no rain came; he told them: let everyone continue fasting overnight; the next day he said: whoever has seen a dream, let him say
R' Elazar of Hagronia: in my dream they read to me: good greetings to the good master from the good Lord, who from His goodness does good to His people
Rava: learn from it that it is a time of favour; they prayed and rain came
a man was sentenced to lashes in Rava's court for relations with a gentile woman; Rava flogged him and he died; word reached King Shapur's house, and he sought to punish Rava
Ifra Hormiz to her son Shapur: have no dealings with the Jews, for whatever they ask of their Master He gives them
Shapur: [they pray and rain comes?] that is because it is the rainy season; let them pray now, in the season of Tammuz, and let rain come
she sent to Rava: direct your mind and pray for rain; he prayed and no rain came
Rava: Master of the world, 'O God, we have heard with our ears, our fathers have told us, the work You did in their days, in days of old' (Ps 44:2) -- and we have not seen it with our eyes!
rain came until the gutters of Mechoza poured into the Tigris
his father appeared to him in a dream: is there anyone who troubles Heaven so much? change your place [of sleep]; he did, and the next day found his bed slashed with knives
Rav Pappa decreed a fast and no rain came; he felt faint, swallowed a bowl of porridge, prayed, and no rain came
Rav Nachman bar Ushpazti: if the master swallows another bowl of porridge, rain will come
he was ashamed and distressed, and rain came

R' Chanina ben Dosa, caught by rain on the road: Master of the world, the whole world is at ease and Chanina is in distress! the rain stopped; at home: the whole world is in distress and Chanina at ease? rain came
Rav Yosef: what did the High Priest's prayer avail against R' Chanina ben Dosa?
as we learned: he [the High Priest] would pray a short prayer in the outer chamber (Yoma 5:1)
Ravin bar Adda and Rava bar Adda, both in Rav Yehuda's name: [he prayed] may it be Your will, Lord our God, that this year be rainy and hot
rather: if [the year is] hot, may it be rainy and dewy; and let not the prayer of travellers enter before You
Rav Acha breih deRava concludes in Rav Yehuda's name: may a ruler not depart from the house of Judah, and may Your people Israel not need to be sustained one from another, nor from another people
every day a heavenly voice goes forth and says: the whole world is sustained for the sake of Chanina My son, and for Chanina My son a kav of carobs suffices from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve
his wife used to heat the oven every Shabbat eve and throw in smoke-making material, out of embarrassment
she had a bad neighbour, who said: I know they have nothing at all -- what is all this? she went and knocked on the door; [the wife] was embarrassed and went into an inner room
a miracle was done for her: [the neighbour] saw the oven full of bread and the trough full of dough, and called: so-and-so, bring a peel, your bread is burning! she said: I too went in for that
a tanna taught: she too had gone in to bring a peel, for she was accustomed to miracles
at his wife's urging (until when shall we suffer so?) he prayed, and something like the palm of a hand came out and gave him one leg of a golden table
she saw in a dream: the righteous will in future eat at a golden table with three legs, and he at a table with two legs
he: are you content that everyone will eat at a complete table and we at a defective one? she: pray that it be taken from you; he prayed and they took it
a tanna taught: the last miracle was greater than the first
for it is learned by tradition that [Heaven] gives and does not take back

one Shabbat eve he saw his daughter sad -- she had lit the Shabbat lamp from vinegar mistaken for oil; he said: my daughter, why does it matter to you? He who told the oil to burn will tell the vinegar to burn
a tanna taught: it went on burning all day, until they took fire from it for havdala
R' Chanina ben Dosa had some goats
told they were causing damage: if they cause damage, let bears eat them; if not, let each bring a bear on its horns in the evening; in the evening each brought a bear on its horns
to a neighbour whose house-beams did not reach: what is your name? Eichu. He said: Eichu, may your beams reach
a tanna taught: they reached until they protruded a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side
and some say: they made them with extensions
Plimo: I saw that house, and its beams protruded a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, and they told me: this is the house R' Chanina ben Dosa roofed by his prayer
and the Sages said: one does not raise small cattle in the Land of Israel

R' Pinchas: a man passed his door and left chickens there; R' Chanina's wife found them, and he told her: do not eat their eggs; they multiplied and distressed them, so he sold them and bought goats with the proceeds; when the man came back and gave a sign, he took the goats -- and these are the goats that brought bears on their horns

R' Elazar ben Pedat was in great poverty; after bloodletting he had nothing to eat but a clove of garlic, fainted and slept; the Sages visiting saw him weeping and laughing, and a ray of fire coming from his forehead
R' Elazar: the Holy One was sitting with me, and I said to Him: until when shall I suffer in this world?
the Holy One: Elazar My son, would you like Me to return the world to its beginning? perhaps you will be born in an hour of sustenance
R' Elazar: all this, and only 'perhaps'? is what remains greater than what I have lived? -- what you have lived; I said: if so, I do not want it
the Holy One: as reward for saying 'I do not want it', I will give you in the world to come thirteen rivers of pure balsam oil, like the Euphrates and the Tigris, to delight in
R' Elazar: this and no more? -- and what shall I give your fellow? -- do I ask from a man who has nothing? He flicked my forehead and said: Elazar My son, My arrows into you
R' Chama bar Chanina decreed a fast and no rain came; told that R' Yehoshua ben Levi decreed one and rain came, he said: this is I, and that is the son of Levi
after a further prayer failed: would you like rain to come for our sake? yes. He said: sky, sky, cover your face! it did not; he said: how brazen is the face of the sky! it covered over and rain came
Levi decreed a fast and no rain came; he said: Master of the world, You went up and sat on high and do not have mercy on Your children; rain came, and he became lame
R' Elazar: a person should never speak harshly toward Above
for a great man spoke harshly toward Above and became lame -- and who was it? Levi
but Levi demonstrated kidda [bowing] before Rebbi and became lame

R' Chiyya bar Luliani heard the clouds say: let us go pour water in Ammon and Moab; he said: Master of the world, when You gave the Torah You offered it to all the nations and they did not accept it, and now You give them rain? pour here! they poured it in their place

R' Chiyya bar Luliani on 'the righteous shall flourish like the palm tree; he shall grow like a cedar in Lebanon' (Ps 92:13): had cedar been said without palm, I would say: as the cedar bears no fruit, so the righteous, God forbid, bears no fruit -- therefore palm is said
had palm been said without cedar, I would say: as the palm's stump does not renew itself, so the righteous, God forbid, does not renew -- therefore cedar is said
the premise of the derasha, as the Gemara reads it at 25b.2 (וארז גזעו מחליף?): the cedar's stump renews itself

one who buys a tree from another to cut down raises [the axe] a handbreadth from the ground and cuts; a sycamore trunk two handbreadths, a virgin sycamore three; reeds and vines from the knot up; palms and cedars he digs down and uproots, because its stump does not renew itself
the baraita's ground: [the palm's and the cedar's] stump does not renew itself
here [in the baraita] we are dealing with the other species of cedar
Rabba bar Huna: there are ten species of cedar, as it says: 'I will set in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, and the myrtle...' (Isa 41:19)

R' Eliezer decreed thirteen fasts on the public and no rain fell; at the last the public began to leave; he said: have you prepared graves for yourselves?! all the people burst into weeping, and rain fell
again R' Eliezer went down before the ark and said twenty-four blessings, and was not answered
R' Akiva went down after him and said: our Father our King, we have no king but You; our Father our King, for Your sake have mercy on us -- and rain fell
the Sages murmured; a heavenly voice went forth and said: not because this one is greater than that one, but because this one forgoes his due and that one does not
how much rain must fall for the public to stop its fasts? the full depth of a plowshare -- R' Meir
and the Sages say: in dry soil, a handbreadth
in medium soil, two handbreadths
in worked soil, three handbreadths
R' Shimon ben Elazar: there is no handbreadth [of rain] from above toward which the deep does not come out three handbreadths
another baraita: [the deep comes out] two handbreadths

R' Elazar: when the water is poured out on the Festival, one deep says to the other: let your waters spring forth, I hear the voice of two friends, as it says: 'deep calls to deep at the voice of Your channels' (Ps 42:8)

Rabbah: I myself saw Ridya, like a calf with parted lips, standing between the lower deep and the upper deep; to the upper deep it says: hold back your waters; to the lower: let your waters spring forth, as it says: 'the blossoms appear on the earth' (Song 2:12)

objections.gloss_en: שחונה מעלייתא היא? אדרבה, גריעותא היא! -- is heat a good thing? on the contrary, it is a detriment
ורבי חנינא בן דוסא מהיכן הוו ליה עזים? והא עני הוי! -- he was poor (a kav of carobs from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve)

answered_by.gloss_en: R' Pinchas's maaseh: the goats were bought with the proceeds of chickens a man had left at his door (= p_pinchas_tarnegolin)

objections.gloss_en: ועוד, אמרו חכמים: אין מגדלין בהמה דקה בארץ ישראל -- how could he keep goats? (kind tanya for the formula אמרו חכמים; see header)

answered_by.gloss_en: the same maaseh: the goats belonged to the man who lost the chickens, and were returned to him; the text gives one answer to the double question and does not spell out how it meets this prong

objections.gloss_en: הא גרמא ליה? והא לוי אחוי קידה קמיה דרבי ואיטלע! -- his lameness came from the kidda he demonstrated before Rebbi

answered_by.gloss_en: הא והא גרמא ליה -- both caused it

objections.gloss_en: וארז גזעו מחליף? והתניא ... בדקלים ובארזים חופר למטה ומשריש, לפי שאין גזעו מחליף

answered_by.gloss_en: הכא במאי עסקינן -- בשאר מיני ארזים (= p_shear_minei_arazim)

objections.gloss_en: והא תניא טפחיים! -- another baraita says the deep comes out two handbreadths

answered_by.gloss_en: לא קשיא: כאן בעבודה, כאן בשאינה עבודה -- here in worked soil, there in unworked soil
